# Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab

Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab (DCS) is the professional cardiology society that serves as the institutional home for the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] (AFDK), Denmark's nationwide clinical quality database for atrial fibrillation. Across both the 2023 and 2024 AFDK annual reports, the database is described as "forankret i Dansk Cardiologisk Selskab (DCS)" — anchored in DCS — with the explicit mandate to help ensure high-quality treatment and care for patients [^src1][^src2]. The 2024 report expands on this mandate, stating that AFDK's role under DCS is also to "ensrette indsatsen for patienter med atrieflimren" (align/standardize efforts for patients with atrial fibrillation) [^src2].

DCS's significance in the corpus is structural rather than operational: it is not shown directing individual clinical decisions, but rather providing the institutional anchor that legitimizes and organizes AFDK as a clinical quality database. This positioning appears in both reports at the point where each document summarizes AFDK's identity and purpose — in the 2023 report, at the close of a chapter on Indicator 8 (structured education programs for newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients), and in the 2024 report, in a section covering patient representatives' perspectives, Hospitalsenhed Midt's patient education practices since 2012, the steering group's membership, and methodological limitations of the database. In both cases, the description of AFDK as a nationwide clinical quality database anchored in DCS (alongside approval from the Danish Health Authority, Sundhedsstyrelsen) frames DCS as the professional body responsible for overseeing quality and consistency in atrial fibrillation care across Denmark.

No further details about DCS's internal structure, leadership, or other activities are given in the available material — its presence in the corpus is limited to this anchoring role for AFDK.
